## Goal
When there is no removal mailbox, the assisted card offers compose links (`compose_links`, `engine/outbox.py:176-187`). The "Email app" link is a `mailto:` URL whose body is percent-encoded with plain `\n` (`%0A`). RFC 6068 requires line breaks in a mailto body to be `%0D%0A`, and Outlook, the mail app many Windows users have, collapses `%0A` into one paragraph. Separately, Windows hands a mailto URL to the mail app through a call that fails or truncates above roughly 2000 characters, and a state-law letter is longer than that. Fix both inside `compose_links`: encode line breaks in the mailto body as `%0D%0A`; if the mailto URL would exceed 1900 characters, return it with the subject only and no body (the card already shows the full letter with a Copy button; do not change the card). The web-mail links (Gmail, Outlook web, Yahoo) keep their current encoding. Keys and the function signature stay.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. For a body with three lines, the "Email app" URL contains `%0D%0A` and no bare `%0A`; the other three links are byte-identical to before for the same input (golden strings captured from main before the change).
2. A body of 500 characters fits and keeps its body; a body of 3000 characters makes the "Email app" link `mailto:<to>?subject=...` with no `body=` and a length under 1900.
3. Subject and address are still percent-encoded safely: a subject with `&`, `?`, `#`, a non-ASCII letter and a space round-trips through `urllib.parse.parse_qs`.
4. A body already containing `\r\n` does not become `%0D%0D%0A` (normalise first).
5. The function never raises for empty strings.
6. `assisted.py` still builds its todo from the links without change (`tests/test_assisted_no_mailbox.py` unchanged and passing); WO-342 tests pass.
